design.question: [scripted] Does the simulated fly's escape response habituate when the looming stimulus repeats quickly?
design.hypothesis: [scripted] Repeating the stimulus every 4 s lowers the escape probability over the later presentations, compared with every 120 s.
design.competing_hypothesis: [scripted] The stimulus stays above the escape threshold however often it repeats.

ir.question: In the digital fly simulator, how does repeating a looming stimulus every 4 s change fraction of the second half of repeated presentations answered by an escape, against the same stimulus every 120 s on matched seeds?
ir.hypothesis: Repeating a looming stimulus every 4 s will decrease late_escape_probability by at least 0.2 fraction on average over matched seeds, compared with the same stimulus every 120 s, in the expected direction in at least 8 of 12 seeds.

observables.description: fraction of repeated presentations answered by an escape
fraction of the second half of repeated presentations answered by an escape
repeated presentations delivered (each waits for the fly to have stood for a set time)
mean interval between successive presentations as delivered
mean angular size of the repeated stimulus at the escape decision
treatment minus control late_escape_probability, averaged over seeds

independent_variables: repeating a looming stimulus every 4 s
controls: baseline arm: the same stimulus every 120 s
matched seeds: each seed places the fly, draws its stimuli and seeds its random streams identically in both arms
fixed apparatus settings, both arms — repeat block: groomHz = 0, takeoffHz = 0, walkStartHz = 0
the fly's version, controller and full parameter table are bound into the plan digest
parameter_constraints: six closed protocols with host-built arenas and stimuli
controller configurations override model parameters only; FlyBody and published values are fixed
the integration settings (physics, sensing and decision periods) are never varied
at most 16000 simulated fly-seconds per experiment
8-16 distinct seeds; the effect must appear in at least half of them

statistical_analysis.method: Matched-seed paired difference of the primary metric; per-seed sign counts; frozen rain-criteria/v1
statistical_analysis.uncertainty: Seeds are independent replicates of one reduced-order model; descriptive only, with no p-value or population inference, and nothing about real flies.

limitations: The digital fly's controller is a reduced-order state machine. It simulates no neurons; its links to Virtual Fly Brain terms are labels, not mechanisms.
Model parameters were chosen for this simulator, not measured or fitted; a result describes the simulator with these values.
Flight is kinematic: no aerodynamics and no MuJoCo physics run in these experiments.
The arena is a box with primitive obstacles and a relative light proxy (not lux); odour, temperature, humidity, airflow and food are not simulated.
Looming stimuli are visual objects only: the fly sees them but cannot touch them, and escape is a giant-fiber proxy, not a modelled neuron.
A result characterizes the simulator and is never empirical evidence about Drosophila.

guards.note: An independent re-simulation reproduces every state hash and measurement

failure.note: No effect or the opposite direction
